findings.location: src/db/org.ts:747-774 (isGenesisOwnerForTenant) and :799-825 (loadAdminContext step 1) vs the T-0605 canonical predicate in src/db/grants-dao.ts:283-313/505-525 (getGrantsForSubject / getRoleSlugsForActor)
findings.issue: Independently confirmed by reading org.ts: both owner-authority resolvers query only `r.slug = 'tenant-owner' AND ra.confirmed_by IS NOT NULL AND <window>` — neither references confirmed2_by or proposed_by at all, unlike the canonical T-0605 predicate `confirmed_by IS NOT NULL AND (confirmed2_by IS NOT NULL OR proposed_by IS NULL)` used everywhere else assignment-activity is checked. This IS a real architectural inconsistency (two parallel authority resolvers, one honoring dual-control, one not) and, if a role_assignment for 'tenant-owner' ever lands with proposed_by SET and confirmed2_by still NULL (a genuine pending 2-approver proposal, one signature down), isGenesisOwnerForTenant/loadAdminContext would already treat that actor as full owner on ONE signature — a real privilege-escalation shape. HOWEVER: exhaustively grepped every `INSERT INTO choros.role_assignment` in src/ (register.ts, reader-grant.ts, rights-intents.ts, grants.ts, user-mgmt.ts) — none of them EVER sets role_assignment.proposed_by to a non-null value today. grants.ts's own role-assignment endpoint computes `isEscalating` from `combineCriticality(roleGrants,...)` compared against ITSELF (fromCrit and toCrit both derived from the identical `roleGrants` query, so `criticalityDiff` is always non-escalating by construction) — its own comment admits this is 'day-1 ... routine one-approver path' and the 2-approver flow for assignments is explicitly deferred future work, not yet wired to any write path. So the gap is real but currently DORMANT — not reachable via any live code path today. The builder's own spec.md §3 and pr-handoff.json risks_for_judge already surface this exact finding, correctly scope it as 'reachability not established, out of scope for T-0764' (a seed-hygiene/CI-honesty task), and recommend it as its own follow-up rather than silently shipping a partial fix. Concur with that scoping — it is not a T-0764 regression (isGenesisOwnerForTenant is pre-existing dev code, untouched by this diff) and forcing a fix into this substrate task would be scope creep past D-064 discipline.
findings.suggestion: File a dedicated follow-up task: either (a) add the `(confirmed2_by IS NOT NULL OR proposed_by IS NULL)` clause to isGenesisOwnerForTenant + loadAdminContext's owner-check so they match the canonical predicate, or (b) add an explicit db-tier test asserting a semi-confirmed tenant-owner role_assignment (proposed_by set, confirmed2_by NULL) is NOT recognized as owner, to lock the invariant BEFORE any future feature wires up assignment-level dual-control and silently inherits this gap. Medium severity — not urgent (no live trigger exists), but should not be forgotten given the explicit code comments already flagging assignment-level escalation as planned future work.
